rounds.text: Conceded: [E6]. United Van Der Horst Ltd demonstrates genuine operational strengthening through a multi-year expansion in its profitability, evidenced by the operating margin rising by three percentage points to reach 38% in March 2026 compared to 35% three years prior [E29]. This core structural improvement in margins unfolds while the stock trades closer to its 52-week low at just 26 percent of its range, presenting a stark disconnect between underlying operational efficiency and market pricing [E5]. Furthermore, the company commands a consistent market capitalisation of ₹ 245 Cr alongside an active dividend yield of 1.13% [E3, E4]. The market's current fixation on backward-looking valuation multiples obscures this margin progression and the inherent stability of a business returning capital to shareholders.

Conceded: [E29]. The bull's reliance on a multi-year operating margin expansion to 38% [E29] ignores the reality that the company's quarterly operating margin actually contracted to 25% in March 2026 compared to 26% in the year-ago quarter [E30]. This recent quarterly compression directly undermines the narrative of unbroken operational strengthening [E30]. Furthermore, pointing to the stock resting at 26% of its 52-week range [E5] does not validate a discount when the valuation remains punishingly expensive at a P/E of 46.9 [E1], or even 59.32x against a sector benchmark of just 23.91x [E6]. The apathetic 1.13% dividend yield [E4] provides negligible income to offset a price-to-book ratio of 4.77x that towers over the sector benchmark of 2.55x [E7]. Finally, this expensive multiple is applied to an asset base that delivers an inferior return on assets of 4.24% compared to the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E8].
